question: In ∆ABC two medians BE and CF intersects at the point O and P, Q are the midpoints of BO and CO respectively. If the length of PQ = 6cm, then the length of FE will be?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In ΔABC, F and E are the midpoints of sides AB and AC, so FE = BC ÷ 2 (by Midpoint Theorem).

In ΔOBC, P and Q are the midpoints of sides OB and OC, so PQ = BC ÷ 2 (by Midpoint Theorem).

Equating both conditions, we find that FE = PQ.

Given the length of PQ is 6 cm, the length of FE must also be 6 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

BE and CF are medians of ΔABC intersecting at point O.

P and Q are the midpoints of BO and CO respectively.

Length of PQ = 6 cm.

**Concept Used:**

**Midpoint Theorem:** The line segment in a triangle joining the midpoints of two sides is parallel to the third side and is exactly half of its length.
